They were housed in the village of Zlokucane. I saw the army there and I saw military vehicles and I saw huge cooking pots and cauldrons so I suppose that this was a quartermaster's unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Tell me what did the Albanian friends of yours tell you about that unit? Were they -- this quartermaster's unit people providing assistance to them?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR PANTIC
utterances.text: Yes, there were no problems there. I had this family favour that I had to return to these people. It was hundred years old or so. I didn't hear about any problems being there, and the priest had played a very prominent role in this communication between the army and the civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Pantic. In paragraph 50 of your statement you spoke about an order issued to somebody by the 7th Infantry Brigade about controlling and regulating traffic, and you spoke about the planned traffic regime that had been ordered at the time. Would you agree with me that planned traffic regime under war circumstances during the state of war or imminent threat of war implies that military vehicles have a priority in traffic?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR PANTIC
utterances.text: Yes. I can tell you that we had these check-points, and I think that this order same from Milomir Cirkovic who was the commander of the 7th Infantry Brigade, and there were also senior officers from the SUP in Pec, and they decided to establish mixed patrols that would patrol in these locations that you mentioned, but they had separate individual tasks. Members of the police -- military police could only control members of police, whereas the policemen could control both civilians and other policemen.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And this planned traffic regime implies that in the state of war military vehicles have priority over civilian vehicles.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR PANTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Pantic, that's all the questions I had for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, if you look at line 22 there in the English transcript, "military police could only control" -- should that be members of the army?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. They could only control members of the army. I apologise. I wasn't following the transcript. Mr. Pantic, that's what you said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You conduct a good cross-examination, so please don't apologise for that. Thank you. Mr. Pantic, you'll now be cross-examined by the Prosecutor. Mr. Oren.

utterances.speaker: MR. OREN
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Pantic.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR PANTIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. OREN
utterances.text: Is it correct to say that you were dismissed as chief of the OUP in Istok?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR PANTIC
utterances.text: What period do you have in mind? You mean 1999, the NATO bombing?

utterances.speaker: MR. OREN
utterances.text: I was referring to October 1999.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR PANTIC
utterances.text: Yes. I received a decision appointing me to a different position.

utterances.speaker: MR. OREN
utterances.text: Do you know why you were dismissed?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR PANTIC
utterances.text: I suppose that it was at the proposal of my chief of secretariat that he gave to the Ministry, and then the ministry took this decision that I didn't meet the requirements at the position I was at the time, and they reassigned me to a different position.

utterances.speaker: MR. OREN
utterances.text: Did you -- did you get any specific reasons why you didn't meet the requirements?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR PANTIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. OREN
utterances.text: And what was the background for your complaints against the MUP, the court proceedings that you told us about earlier?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR PANTIC
utterances.text: I believed that it was unfair that I was reassigned to a different position.

utterances.speaker: MR. OREN
utterances.text: Were you demoted?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR PANTIC
utterances.text: I haven't received interpretation. Yes, I was demoted and my salary was reduced.

utterances.speaker: MR. OREN
utterances.text: And what was the outcome of the complaint against the MUP?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR PANTIC
utterances.text: The court ruled in my favour, and I was returned to my original position. The whole case lasted two years, and I won in the end.

utterances.speaker: MR. OREN
utterances.text: During your court case did you then hear some particulars concerning why you didn't meet the requirements as chief of the Istok OUP?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR PANTIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't know the details. I simply knew that a session was at Mount Kapaonik and Vlajko Stojiljkovic, the minister took that decision. That's what I was told.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CHOWHAN
utterances.text: I'm sorry to intervene here. Could you kindly apprise me of the fact whether you got no information about what was against you while you were litigating in the court and you won the case?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know how to explain that to you. Once you receive a decision the decision says that you are appointed to a different position where you are more likely to meet the requirements than at your previous position. That was the statement of reasons in the decision.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You may have misunderstood that question. You had a court case that lasted two years. During that time was there no reason given?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. They simply challenged my case, my petition. They didn't provide their own reasons for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Is that why you won?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Oren.

utterances.speaker: MR. OREN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. OREN
utterances.text: In paragraph 48 of your statement you refer to an order of the 69th Military Territorial Detachment of 1st April, 1999, concerning establishment of a staff at Istok. If we could have 6D117 in e-court. This is the order that you referred to in your -- in your statement, and in item 1 we see that it order that all government organs of Istok are placed under command of the 69th Military Territorial Detachment Istok, and in item 2 orders -- and item 2 orders the formation of a staff for Istok and who is to be member of this staff. If you could go to the next page of both the English and the B/C/S version. You see that an item is called (k). Or perhaps the B/C/S version is on the first page. No, it's on the second page as well. We see that (k) states that: "For public law and order and crime prevention, fire-fighting and other tasks under the jurisdiction of the MUP, chief of the Istok OUP and his deputy Istok OUP police commander." Now, the chief of the Istok OUP, is that you?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR PANTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OREN
utterances.text: Now, if you could go to P1982. If we could have that up in e-court. Now, this is an order of 12th April 1999 by the 7th Infantry Brigade Command signed by Milomir Cirkovic concerning organisation of life and work in the zone of combat operations. Have you seen this order before?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR PANTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OREN
utterances.text: Did you receive it straight after 12th April 1999?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR PANTIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. When members of the 7th Infantry Brigade arrived.

utterances.speaker: MR. OREN
utterances.text: Okay. And in item 1 it is ordered to establish a staff in Istok for the organisation of life and work in the zone of combat operation. Is there any relation between this order and the one that we just looked at as referred to as 6D117?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR PANTIC
utterances.text: Well, there is an obvious difference. Mr. Cirkovic formulated it as it should be unlike the commander of the 69th platoon. I don't know. This second paragraph where it speaks about the police. He said their regular duties which we normally perform in war and in peace taking care of law and order and everything else that falls under the purview of the Ministry of the Interior. Although you see that here towards the end he says the security of property, he said that I was in charge of it, and the inspector listed here, Ranko Dizdarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OREN
utterances.text: But is this the same staff as we just saw, or is this another staff? Did it exist two such staff in Istok at this time?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR PANTIC
utterances.text: No, no. The previous staff was disbanded once this was issued. As soon as he arrived, Mr. Cirkovic cancelled, annulled the order of his predecessor, the commander of the 69th Detachment and other people were brought in. Normally there would be 10 to 15 of us at meetings.

utterances.speaker: MR. OREN
utterances.text: You already yourself pointed out that you were responsible for the protection of property and for public order, peace, crime prevention, fire protection, and other tasks within the responsibility of the MUP. Now, is there any difference between your tasks described in this document compared to the other one that we saw?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR PANTIC
utterances.text: In the previous document there is no paragraph mentioning safety and security of property and so on, but otherwise --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat the last sentence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Could you repeat the last part of that answer, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said that there are similarities in the order issued by Mr. Cirkovic, but in the first order of the 69th Platoon there is no mention of me being in charge of safety and security of property, me and inspector Ranko Svilarevic. This order is formulated somewhat differently in relation to the previous one issued by the platoon commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. OREN
utterances.text: Did you ever attend meetings with this staff?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR PANTIC
utterances.text: I did. Initially I attended the meetings of the staff when the commander of the 69th Platoon was there, and then I had a partial conflict with him and a partial one with the president of the municipality. I didn't want to go to these meetings. I informed my superiors about that, and my superiors sent Colonel Radovan Paponjak a bit later on to coordinate the work between the staff headed by the president of the municipality on the one hand and the army and the Ministry of the Interior on the other hand.

utterances.speaker: MR. OREN
utterances.text: Also in paragraph 48 of this statement you refer to serious rows between you and the commander of the 69th Military Territorial Detachment. Now, what was the name of that commander?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR PANTIC
utterances.text: Milosavljevic Princip.

utterances.speaker: MR. OREN
utterances.text: Could you be a bit more specific about these serious rows, as you call it? Could you explain to us what these were?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR PANTIC
utterances.text: Well, from this point of view the rows were reflected in the following: As soon as the state of war and mobilisation were declared, he mobilised people, and he put them up, say, in kindergartens in the centre of town, in schools. I advised him to the effect that that was not a good idea, that the police would handle this. They would find a different location. He refused that. He said that he was the commander and that he would do what he thought was right. Then we had this serious difference, and I asked my superiors to set up these joint military patrols. On the first evening he gave me three men, and I knew that they had had a criminal record and of course that they would not act in accordance with the law, and they would not enforce the law properly in terms of checking vehicles and persons. He simply would not give up on this, on these orders, persistently trying to subordinate me. I personally think that I did the right thing then from this point of view as I sit here, I still think it was a good idea that I did not allow him to subordinate me; otherwise all sorts of things would have happened, things that would not have been right for the population or anyone else for that matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. OREN
utterances.text: In paragraph 51 of your statement you also refers to daily conflicts also with Princip deputy president of the Municipal Assembly Malisa Perovic. Did your conflict with the president of the Municipal Assembly relate to the same topics as with the commander or were they of a different nature?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR PANTIC
utterances.text: No. There were some other situations, some other things as well, because we were processing Perovic and he was supposed to be processed around the 23rd concerning the crimes he committed in relation to humanitarian aid. These were enormous amounts of money, millions. I still have the documents. We got orders from the ministry directly. I think this is a dispatch from General Djordjevic that all materiel and technical resources in relation to which there were thefts, looting, et cetera, that all of this should be documented and that the documents should be compiled, and once an inventory was made this should be handed over to the Municipal Staff. However, the president of the municipality wanted all of this to be handed over to him on the very same day without any records whatsoever. So what we would do during the course of one day or the financial inspectors or the market inspectors, because we never went to a shop, a store, anywhere without being accompanied by the market inspectors, crime police as well of the OUP and the financial police. We went to shops and stores that had been looted. I'll give you an example. If some medicine was taken from a pharmacy, it was always handed over to --

utterances.speaker: MR. OREN
utterances.text: Sorry to interrupt you, but I think you have answered my question.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR PANTIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: What is the answer to your question? Is it yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MR. OREN
utterances.text: I think that the way he describes it is also of another nature as the one with the command because it also relates to other things.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You're right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OREN
utterances.text: And you may mention the crimes concerning -- in relation to humanitarian aid. Did you carry out investigation in that, in relation to that?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR PANTIC
utterances.text: I don't understand your question. Crimes related to humanitarian aid, you have to explain this to me. What kind of action we took, is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: MR. OREN
utterances.text: Yes. You said of the subject of humanitarian aid being misused. My question is were an investigation in relation to that carried out?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR PANTIC
utterances.text: I don't know. All the documentation in relation to this was forwarded to Belgrade. We did establish a great many things that were unlawful. Flour, for example. I'll give you the example of flour that was part of this humanitarian aid, was sold to Albanians who had bakeries in the territory of the municipality of Istok. And also material and technical resources. Furniture, everything that was sent from Serbia as humanitarian aid to Kosovo, cured meat and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. OREN
utterances.text: When you say you did establish a great many things, was that through investigation?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR PANTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OREN
utterances.text: And were these investigation concerning specific persons?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR PANTIC
utterances.text: The president of the municipality took part in this, and the leaders mentioned at the very beginning. The head of district of the SPS and the head of this committee, whatever it was called, for the Pec district.

utterances.speaker: MR. OREN
utterances.text: This investigation, was that the reason why Paponjak came to Istok 12 April 1999?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR PANTIC
utterances.text: No, no. We're talking about 1998, up until the 23rd of May, 1999. That is to say all of 1998, all the way up to the 23rd of March, 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. OREN
utterances.text: So this investigation had nothing to do about the fact that Paponjak came to Istok in April?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR PANTIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. OREN
utterances.text: Now, what kind of authority did Paponjak have at Istok OUP?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR PANTIC
utterances.text: He was sent without any kind of decision of appointment. He was sent by officers outranking me to channel the work of the military and the police, and after a while, since I kept refusing to attend these meetings of the staff, he ordered me to accompany him. I observed that, and up until the 11th of June we regularly went to attend meetings together, meetings of the staff, that is, and meetings of the commanders -- of the commander of the 7th Brigade wherever necessary.

utterances.speaker: MR. OREN
utterances.text: What kind of authority did he have in relation to you? Could he order you? Could he give you orders?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR PANTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OREN
utterances.text: So in practice Paponjak replaced you as chief of the Istok OUP; right?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR PANTIC
utterances.text: Well, he didn't replace me. He coordinated this work. He outranked me anyway and he could issue orders to me regardless of whether he had come to Istok or whether he was in Pec. In terms of the hierarchy, he was above me and he could issue orders to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. OREN
utterances.text: So it was Paponjak who supervised the OUP, right, of Istok?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR PANTIC
utterances.text: Well, I used the word "coordinate." That is coordination. When I didn't manage to get something done, then he would do it, and then we acted together in this coordination with the local civilian organs of authority, the president of the municipality and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. OREN
utterances.text: Is it true that it was only on paper that you were chief of the Istok OUP?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR PANTIC
utterances.text: Well, it can be put that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. OREN
utterances.text: And is it also right that after Paponjak came you could no longer issue orders or instructions to the OUP in Istok?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR PANTIC
utterances.text: Well, I could when I could give -- get authority from him, but I could also issue some orders independently. It's -- well, this was a question of coordination, although of course it is only natural that he was ahead of me.

utterances.speaker: MR. OREN
utterances.text: Could we have P1721 up in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. OREN
utterances.text: Now, you have referred to this document in paragraph 54 of your statement, and you have already been asked some questions about it. At that time, that is 14th of April, 1999, were you familiar with the alleged existence of camps in Istok where Siptar refugees were accommodated as referred to in the first paragraph of this document?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR PANTIC
utterances.text: I put these people up there. They were not in a camp. Most of them had houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. OREN
utterances.text: When you refer to "these people," are you then in item -- item 1 of the first page where it reference to around 544 people being accommodated in the elementary school in the village of Suvi Lukavac?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR PANTIC
utterances.text: No, no. In this area -- the areas that are referred to in the first paragraph up here. These are displaced persons from Uka [phoen], Mojstir, Susica, those villages, and Sinaj in part. What you are talking about is the territory of the local commune of Djurakovac. That's on the road between Kosovska Mitrovica and Pec.

utterances.speaker: MR. OREN
utterances.text: What was the village of Suvi Lukavac, was that within the Istok municipality?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR PANTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OREN
utterances.text: And did you know about this group of refugees, these 544 persons that is referred to here? Did you know about that?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR PANTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OREN
utterances.text: And why was this group of persons situated in this elementary school?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR PANTIC
utterances.text: Well, there was no room elsewhere. In this group that was in Lukavac, for instance, it wasn't only Albanians from Istok that were there. There were also some from the area of Kosovska Mitrovica. This was the most appropriate location for their accommodation, because there were operations taking place and this was the safest place for them to be.

utterances.speaker: MR. OREN
utterances.text: Who made the decision to accommodate them in this school?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR PANTIC
utterances.text: The Municipal Staff was directly in charge of that, a woman, Ljubinka Perovic, for that matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. OREN
utterances.text: Now, this report is dated 14th of April, 1999. Do you know for how long this group of refugees had been in the elementary school?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR PANTIC
utterances.text: Not in 1992. Perhaps you're referring to 1999. I don't know. I don't know how long they stayed there. They were in this school for a couple of days.

utterances.speaker: MR. OREN
utterances.text: Do you know where they went afterwards?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR PANTIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. OREN
utterances.text: Now, the second paragraph of item 1, it refers to 221 refugees on the outskirts of Istok. Do you have any knowledge about this group of refugees?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR PANTIC
utterances.text: I know. I took that group in on orders from my superior from Pec, and I put them up -- well, the rest were my friends, and they were from the Lushaj family. They were near the high school there and they had family houses there and there were houses opposite them. I had this dilemma there. This was a new problem for me. In addition to the order made by my chief of inspection [as interpreted], I gave myself the liberty of phoning General Lukic and consulting him about this. My instructions were is to consult the members of the military, whether they could go home or not, and if not then they could be put up where I had put them up in the first place.

utterances.speaker: MR. OREN
utterances.text: And what did General Lukic tell you?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR PANTIC
utterances.text: General Lukic told me to talk to the members of the military. If they are not involved in any kind of operations in this zone of responsibility of theirs then these persons could go back home and if they do then this proposal that I made to put them up there because these were their family homes in Istok then I could leave them there and that is what I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just one intervention to avoid any doubts. On page 60, line 4 -- actually 5, it says chief of inspection, and it should be chief of SUP. I think that the witness said so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Could you, Mr. Pantic, deal with that again. You were being asked about the group of refugees, the 221 refugees, and you said that you consulted General Lukic. What were the circumstances in which you consulted General Lukic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You mean how it was that I consulted him? Over the telephone you mean. This was a new problem for me the one that had cropped up, and my orders were from my superior in Pec that I should return these people to their homes. Since actions were under way, I thought that I should consult General Lukic. I consulted him, and the answer I got was that I should first consult the members of the military to ask whether they had some kind of activity there since this was their zone of responsibility, if I could not return them to their homes then I could leave them somewhere else, but my proposal was since most of them had family homes in the villages where they were staying and on the outskirts of Istok. So that's where I put them up, in that area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Oren.

utterances.speaker: MR. OREN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. OREN
utterances.text: Do you know how long this grouped stayed on the outskirts of Istok?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR PANTIC
utterances.text: Until the end of the war, until the end of the bombing, the very end. It grew bigger. At the end it was about 250 people.

utterances.speaker: MR. OREN
utterances.text: Now, these people, these 250 people you refer to, they were in fact detained, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR PANTIC
utterances.text: No, no, no, no. I kept insisting at staff meetings -- I mean, they walked around town. I initiated that, and they were allowed to visit doctors at the health centres.

utterances.speaker: MR. OREN
utterances.text: Now, in the same paragraph it is also referred to the fact that this group of refugees that were intercepted by a group of Specials, it's called here. Do you know what Specials here refers to?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR PANTIC
utterances.text: You mean on the road near the village of Rausovic? That's the road from Pec to Decani. I don't know exactly who or what.

utterances.speaker: MR. OREN
utterances.text: But there is a reference to a group of Specials there. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR PANTIC
utterances.text: I see that, but I don't know what group of Specials this is. I really have no idea.

utterances.speaker: MR. OREN
utterances.text: But were you aware that these people were intercepted by such a group and that they had seized vehicles, money, and jewellery from the group of refugees that stayed there?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR PANTIC
utterances.text: No, no. I was just told to take these people in and to have them put up at their homes, and if that is not possible then I should find a place where they could be put up.

utterances.speaker: MR. OREN
utterances.text: Did you have any contact with the commission in its work related to these alleged camps?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR PANTIC
utterances.text: What commission?

utterances.speaker: MR. OREN
utterances.text: This commission that was established pursuant to order of 13 of April, 1999, P1917 like we just saw, the commission that have compiled this report that you have in front of you.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR PANTIC
utterances.text: On the 14th, on the 14th of April, that day my grandfather died and I had to make a statement regrettably. There wasn't even enough understanding in view of that. I made a statement, and I had a bit of a discussion with Mr. Djakovic, and I tried to explain to him that what he was saying was untruthful and that it would not be a good thing to have things go that way, but obviously he had his own ideas about this and things turned out the way they did. Later on I made a statement six hours after my grandfather's funeral. I made a statement for about six hours. I enclosed a great many documents where I refuted every word that had to do with the work of the OUP and myself personally, anything that had to do with the commission of crimes and any kind of action that could disrupt the peace that was supposed to prevail in the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. OREN
utterances.text: This interview or statement, was it also related to the alleged camps?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR PANTIC
utterances.text: No, no. That was established on the spot. Otherwise, I know where this was brewed and how this attempt was made to plant this on me. When people came there, they realised that there was no camp there. These 250 people still communicate with me to this day, after the 14th of April as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. OREN
utterances.text: What do you mean that this was attempt was made to plant this on you? What do you mean by is that?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR PANTIC
utterances.text: This is a personal matter. Somebody was bothered by the fact that I was there at that point in time, like the president of the municipality. It didn't suit him to have me in that position at all. I am not a yes-man. I act in accordance with the law and with orders that are issued to me, but I was not a political yes-man.

utterances.speaker: MR. OREN
utterances.text: But what was tried to plant on you? Was that in relation to these alleged camps?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR PANTIC
utterances.text: Well, that's it. That's it. And a great many other things too. For example, you see here towards the end that I received orders from my superiors and not from members of the military. That is wrong. These were orders that the president of the municipality tried to issue to me. I didn't want his orders. I didn't want to accept that at all. And I did not act arbitrarily. No member of the MUP ever arbitrarily acted -- well, you know, can I explain this? Mr. Prosecutor, am I allowed to explain this a bit further, because it does have to do with what we're talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. OREN
utterances.text: I think we'll come to that, so if you can just answer the following questions I think we'll come to that.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR PANTIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. OREN
utterances.text: Just one last question concerning the alleged camps. The initial order is issued 13th of April, P1720, as we've seen. And this report in front of you is dated 14th of April. Now, it's not possible, is it, in such a short time for a commission to conclude with certainty that such camps did not exist and never had existed in the whole territory of Istok municipality?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR PANTIC
utterances.text: I claim with full responsibility that no such thing existed in the whole territory of Istok municipality, and the camps were not established by the members of the MUP or the members of the military. So I stand by my statement that that was the situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. OREN
utterances.text: But my question was if it were possible for a commission, this commission that we have seen had been established to conclude in such a short time.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR PANTIC
utterances.text: They were put up in the centre of Istok so --

utterances.speaker: MR. OREN
utterances.text: Could you answer my question, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think that this calls for speculation whether some other commission could conclude something. The witness already answered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: He hasn't answered about the commission, though, has he? Are you saying that there's something omitted from the transcript? Did you say, Mr. Pantic, something about they could check in five minutes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That does not seem to have been reflected in the transcript. On the matter of speculation, there's no foundation in that objection. This is a matter that the witness familiar with the area and the subject could deal with.

utterances.speaker: MR. OREN
utterances.text: Do you want me to repeat my question, Mr. Pantic?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR PANTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OREN
utterances.text: In your opinion, is it possible for this commission in one day's work to establish that there were no camps and never had existed any camps in the whole territory of Istok municipality?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR PANTIC
utterances.text: I repeat once again and I claim with full responsibility that the MUP or the army did not have any camps in the territory of the municipality of Istok, and whoever wanted to establish this could do so. Whoever wished to do so could go there and see.

utterances.speaker: MR. OREN
utterances.text: So the answer to my question is yes, one day was sufficient for the commission.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR PANTIC
utterances.text: Sufficient.

utterances.speaker: MR. OREN
utterances.text: Now, if we go to part 2 of this report, item 2, it regards the functioning of the system of defence and organs of authority in the Istok municipality. So if we could go to page 2 of the English version, and it is the penultimate paragraph on page 1 of the B/C/S version. Now, the first sentence says: "After familiarising himself with the order, the chief of the Istok OUP stated that it did not apply to him and that he received orders only from his superiors." You remember which order is referred to here? Do you know which order is referred to here?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR PANTIC
utterances.text: I received orders from the president of the municipality, not the Staff Commander. I told president of municipality that his orders were not valid for me and that I refused to accept his orders. That was at the time when he was deputy of the Staff Commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. OREN
utterances.text: Now, if we continue to read, it says: "On his order, members of the MUP entered private houses and shops without authorisation and took goods from them ..." When you comment on this in your statement in paragraph 54, you say that you or the police don't give orders. So then I'll ask you if you instructed, asked, instigate, or otherwise suggested to members of your OUP to enter private houses and shops and take goods from them?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR PANTIC
utterances.text: This is not true. What is stated here is not true. A dispatch arrived from the Ministry of the Interior, chief of the sector, to the effect that materiel and technical equipment were never -- it is established that people who are prone to theft could get their hands on them, that that needed to be warehoused if the owners were not there. So afterwards when all of these goods and property were listed by the MUP, then this was to be turned over to the local staff, and a problem came about because the president of the municipality wanted this to be given to him on a daily basis without any record, and I didn't want to do that. This was not provided to the court, but I do have in my archives a list listing down every single item, every medicine that was found by members of the MUP and listed. If for example Marinko in Tripkovic [phoen] was in charge of those issues by the staff in charge of medication, then all of the medication was listed down and he signed a list stating that this was turned over to the health centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. OREN
utterances.text: I'm sorry to interrupt you, but I think you asked -- you answered my question.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR PANTIC
utterances.text: I want to explain everything so that nothing remains unclarified as to what was done, because we had situations when Albanians, say, had a dental practice and they wanted to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Pantic. Mr. Pantic, your job here in the system that we have in this Tribunal is to answer the particular questions that you're asked. It's not simply to tell us what you consider you ought to tell us. If you think that it's necessary to say something to explain an answer then that's fine, but that's the limit, the extent to which you should elaborate. Mr. Oren.

utterances.speaker: MR. OREN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. OREN
utterances.text: Now, concerning -- stated here that on your order members of the MUP entered private houses and shops without authorisation and took goods from them. Now, where did the commission get this kind of information from?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR PANTIC
utterances.text: I don't know where this information came from, but that's not true, because not a single item could be carried away unless a team was established comprising one policeman, market inspector, and financial inspector. So nobody could arbitrarily order anyone to enter somebody else's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. OREN
utterances.text: But why would the commission put forward such allegation if they were not well founded?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR PANTIC
utterances.text: You have to ask that of them. I truly can't answer that, nor did I know that the commission wrote this down. And if I may expand. I read part of this in the daily Politika in 2000 or in 2001, and also in the Vojska magazine, and I addressed both ministers, that of the defence and that of the interior, to refute that, and they did not allow me to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OREN
utterances.text: If we go to the next paragraph of the document it states that: "Despite warnings from the staff that the collection of goods was not in his jurisdiction, the chief of the OUP said that he was collecting the goods for his unit ..."

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR PANTIC
utterances.text: No. This is not true. This is not something that I know. I simply didn't have this. My unit was mostly engaged. Fifty people from my unit were engaged in PJP. So this is not true. I performed my work. Everything that I did, I did with some 20 to 25 policemen.

utterances.speaker: MR. OREN
utterances.text: Did you receive such warnings as they are described from the staff?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR PANTIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. OREN
utterances.text: But were there any goods stored at Istok OUP?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR PANTIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. OREN
utterances.text: What about the collected goods that you told us about? Where was that stored?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR PANTIC
utterances.text: It was warehoused at the department store in Istok and after the list was drawn up of inventory it was turned over to the person designated by the president of the municipality, Vlajkovic Desimir. So anything that had been collected in terms of property, everything was turned over to the president of municipality, that is to say president of the staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. OREN
utterances.text: And what about the last sentence in that paragraph stating that: "He also said that he had secured goods for his unit for a year." It's true, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR PANTIC
utterances.text: No. And there are documents confirming this. If you're interested, I can provide them.

utterances.speaker: MR. OREN
utterances.text: Accordance to this report, you said that he also said, that means that you said, that he had secured goods for his unit for a year." Did you say this to the commission?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR PANTIC
utterances.text: I don't know who uttered those words. Everything that you're showing me now is quite new to me. I haven't had occasion to see that until now and to defend myself from these allegations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Who -- who from the commission spoke to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I remember that on behalf of the MUP there was General Momir Stojanovic, Blagoje Pesic, and then a person who introduced himself as Milan Djakovic and I can't rather the other people.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So did they interview you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, very briefly. When I came back from my grandfather's funeral they talked to me for half an hour only and then Blagoje Pesic remained and I gave a statement to him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Oren.

utterances.speaker: MR. OREN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. OREN
utterances.text: I just want to ask you something in relation to what you said earlier concerning the 250 people in the outskirts of Istok. Now, on page 63, line 10, you said that, "These 250 people still communicate with me to this day after the 14th of April as well." Do you then mean that you have contact with all these 250 people today?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR PANTIC
utterances.text: Not with all of them, just with some of them, some individuals.

utterances.speaker: MR. OREN
utterances.text: And how many of these 250 people you still communicate with?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR PANTIC
utterances.text: Well, I wouldn't be able to say. With a lot of them. Naturally some five to six. Those are the people that I grew up with, the people that I have lived with for 39 years.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Oren, are these the same people as are referred to in the report as 220 people?

utterances.speaker: MR. OREN
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, it is. And he said that it grew to 250, and that's why I'm referring to 250.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OREN
utterances.text: If we go back to the document in -- in front of you, you see that in -- you also refer to in the next paragraph that you on your own initiative distributed the collected goods to members of the OUP, supposedly along with the written record and the approval of the superior officer Colonel Boro Vlahovic. Indeed did you distribute collected goods to the members of your OUP? Did you?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR PANTIC
utterances.text: What we gave away, five kilos of rice or so, that had arrived from the Pec SUP via them, so no way we could have given anything of the sort. Five kilos of rice can last you a month, not a year.

utterances.speaker: MR. OREN
utterances.text: And in the next paragraph it also states that: "It is our assessment that the personal conflict is involved between the OUP chief and the president of Istok municipality ..." Is that the same personal conflict as you have already explained to us?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR PANTIC
utterances.text: I keep repeating to you that this is only a report of Major-General Milan Djakovic. Other members of the commission did not sign to this, did not confirm that this was true, relevant, or that this is how it was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Please just deal with the question. We've -- we know your position on that. What is the personal conflict that's being referred to here?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I've already explained this a number of times. He asked me to commit crimes on his behalf, and I refused to do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Oren.

utterances.speaker: MR. OREN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. OREN
utterances.text: And in the last sentence -- or at the end of that paragraph it also refers to a conflict with officers of the Pec SUP and the representative of the Pec district. Did you know -- do you have any knowledge of this?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR PANTIC
utterances.text: I've already said that this has to do with humanitarian aid from 1998 until 23rd of March 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. OREN
utterances.text: So also that other conflict that is referred to in that paragraph relates to the same subject as your personal conflict with the president of Istok municipality?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR PANTIC
utterances.text: He used his newly created position, and he tried to impose this I suppose both to the army and to my superiors.

utterances.speaker: MR. OREN
utterances.text: In the next paragraph it again repeats the accusation of crimes committed. I'll not go into that, but at the very end it says that: "... and an investigation should be conducted in order to establish the facts." Now, did such an investigation take place?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR PANTIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. OREN
utterances.text: And in the next paragraph it is stated that there are problems regarding poor coordination which is leading to a parallel command and that: "The criminal activities and incomplete functioning of the security system in the territory of the municipality are also a consequence of that." Do you know what criminal activities are referred to here?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR PANTIC
utterances.text: I don't know. It wasn't specified which acts, committed by whom, where, how.

utterances.speaker: MR. OREN
utterances.text: Now, in your statement you say that it is obvious that Djakovic alone wrote this report without the participation of the other commission members. Now, how can you say that?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR PANTIC
utterances.text: I can tell that based on the signature. No other members of the commission signed it except for Major-General Djakovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OREN
utterances.text: Yeah, he signed it, that's correct, but does that mean that he was alone in drafting, writing it?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR PANTIC
utterances.text: I suppose so considering that other people did not sign this confirming that they approved his report.

utterances.speaker: MR. OREN
utterances.text: Are you by this suggesting that -- simply the fact that he was the only one who signed the report, or do you also suggest that he was the only one who did some work in relation to this commission?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR PANTIC
utterances.text: He wasn't able to work alone. If this was a multi-member commission, then this should list the president of the commission and other members. So Momo Stojanovic's signature should be there as well as other signature of other members of the commission confirming that they agree with the report by Djakovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OREN
utterances.text: But in your contacts with the commission was it only Djakovic that you were in contact with or also other members of the commission?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR PANTIC
utterances.text: All members of the commission. There were a number of people whom I didn't know from the army and from the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. OREN
utterances.text: Now, in your opinion all these allegations against you in this document from the commission, they are wrong; right?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR PANTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OREN
utterances.text: So you think the commission didn't do a very good and thorough job on this point?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR PANTIC
utterances.text: I'm not referring to the commission. I'm referring to the president of the commission. We don't have the opinion of the entire commission. We only have the opinion of the president of the commission.

utterances.speaker: MR. OREN
utterances.text: But you think that the president of the commission, then, did -- didn't do a very good and thorough job on this point?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR PANTIC
utterances.text: I think he didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. OREN
utterances.text: But if he did that in regards to the conclusion related to you, how couldn't that also be the same regarding his work in relation to the existence of camps in the territory of Istok?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR PANTIC
utterances.text: I can't say anything about the general, because I simply don't know. I can only answer questions pertaining to what I see in front of me.

utterances.speaker: MR. OREN
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Now, in --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Oren, where are you in the overall context of your --

utterances.speaker: MR. OREN
utterances.text: I have a few more topics that I would like to address with this witness, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And how long is that likely to take?

utterances.speaker: MR. OREN
utterances.text: Fifteen, 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You have already had, I think, what would normally be appropriate in this context, but it is an extensive statement with recently added documents, so the position would warrant allowing a little more time, but it can't be today. We're now at 1.45. So, Mr. Pantic, I'm afraid we've to bring our proceedings for today to an end because another court occupies this courtroom later. That means you need to return here tomorrow to complete your evidence, and that will be at 9.00 tomorrow morning. Meanwhile, it's a strict rule that you have no communication with anyone at all about any aspect of the evidence in this case. Please bear that strictly in mind. You may now leave the courtroom with the usher and we'll see you again tomorrow at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 3rd day of April, 2008, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.45 p.m.,
